note_fixes: Proverbs 8:27–29: keep the note 'I was there when He established the heavens' (v27, exact).
concepts.why: Passages against the name, and the original arbitrates (Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran, Reformed, biblical-theological, secular scholar): verses 30-31 say Wisdom was 'a skilled craftsman at His side' rejoicing, which is about Wisdom's delight, not the LORD founding the earth by wisdom. The Hebrew word behind 'skilled craftsman' (amon) is disputed, so the displayed verse rests on one translation's choice, and it is the very clause on which readers part over what Wisdom is. Verses 27-29 hold the concept in full; the rest is longer than the concept needs.

concepts.name: A throne is established through righteousness
concepts.why: Name against passages: 'By me kings reign' is Wisdom's own claim in Proverbs 8:15-16 and no other passage here says that kings reign by Wisdom; 16:10, 16:12-13, 20:28, 25:4-5, 29:4 and 29:14 say a king's throne stands by righteousness, justice and loving devotion, and 1 Kings 3:28 shows it. The BSB's words in 16:12 ('a throne is established through righteousness'; 25:5 'established in righteousness') name what the passages share and keep 8:15-16 inside it (just laws, governing justly). Under the present name six of eight passages say less than the name, and it reads as a claim about divine right of rulers, where a free church (Anabaptist-leaning) or a secular reader would object. No passage is dropped; every note stays exact.

note_fixes: Job 42:2–5: keep the note 'My ears had heard of You, but now my eyes have seen You' (v5, exact).
concepts.why: The original arbitrates (secular scholar, Jewish readers of the Hebrew), in the same way as Job 13:15 and 19:26 in round one: Job 42:6 'I despise myself, and I repent in dust and ashes' rests on a disputed Hebrew clause (the verb has no object, and 'repent' may equally be read 'am comforted' or 'relent'), and the BSB follows one choice. The concept (the LORD answers, Job answers) is fully held by 42:2-5, which end on the note. Verse 6 is also where Christian traditions part on what Job repents of.

Name against passages: the name is the image of the breath (Ps 144:4, 39:5, Job 7:7) and the passing shadow or flower (Job 14:1-2); Genesis 3:19 and Psalm 103:14 say 'dust', a different image, so two of six passages say what the name does not. Dust is already carried by Ecclesiastes 3:19-20 (concept 26), and Psalm 103:14 sits naturally with 103:15-16 in concept 28 (extend that passage to Psalm 103:14-16). Genesis 3:19 also brings in a reading of death as the consequence of the fall, on which Orthodox, Catholic, Reformed and secular readers differ, under a name that does not say it.

secondary_or_links: Secondary 'Wisdom → much sorrow': Ecclesiastes 2:15 ('What then have I gained by being wise?') does not say sorrow and shares only the word 'wise'; keep Ecclesiastes 1:18 alone (2:15 is already in concept 26).
Concept 28: if concept 27 loses Psalm 103:14, extend its Psalm 103:15-16 passage to Psalm 103:14-16 (note stays 'As for man, his days are like grass', exact in v15).

Links: dropping Messiah/Christology is acceptable and the safer choice, since the link would otherwise read as Old Testament wisdom pointing to Christ; no other change. The last concept (35) was re-checked: all notes exact, in-theme words of hope, nothing dark softened or left out, and the hard concepts (21, 25, 26, 27, 22) remain as their own.
